datasets.name: adopt_overall
queryLines:
SELECT
  score_pct        AS overall_pct,
  grade            AS overall_grade,
  points,
  max_points,
  active_count,
  minimal_count,
  none_count,
  not_measurable_count,
  coverage_pct,
  run_ts
FROM assessment.results.adoption_section_score
WHERE run_id = (SELECT run_id FROM assessment.results.adoption_section_score ORDER BY run_ts DESC LIMIT 1) AND section = 'OVERALL'

datasets.name: adopt_sections
queryLines:
SELECT
  section,
  score_pct,
  grade,
  points,
  max_points,
  active_count,
  minimal_count,
  none_count,
  not_measurable_count,
  coverage_pct,
  weight
FROM assessment.results.adoption_section_score
WHERE run_id = (SELECT run_id FROM assessment.results.adoption_section_score ORDER BY run_ts DESC LIMIT 1) AND section <> 'OVERALL'

datasets.name: adopt_checks
queryLines:
SELECT
  section,
  check_id,
  check_name,
  CASE label
    WHEN 'ACTIVE'  THEN 'In real use'
    WHEN 'MINIMAL' THEN 'Barely used'
    WHEN 'NONE'    THEN 'Not used'
    ELSE label
  END AS usage_level,
  score,
  COALESCE(value_display, '') AS measured,
  COALESCE(detail, '') AS detail,
  CASE WHEN measurable = FALSE THEN 'not observable'
       WHEN error IS NOT NULL THEN 'query failed'
       ELSE 'measured' END AS measurable
FROM assessment.results.adoption_check_history
WHERE run_id = (SELECT run_id FROM assessment.results.adoption_section_score ORDER BY run_ts DESC LIMIT 1)
ORDER BY check_id

datasets.name: adopt_label_mix
queryLines:
SELECT
  CASE label
    WHEN 'ACTIVE'  THEN 'In real use'
    WHEN 'MINIMAL' THEN 'Barely used'
    ELSE 'Not used'
  END                AS usage_level,
  COUNT(*)           AS capabilities
FROM assessment.results.adoption_check_history
WHERE run_id = (SELECT run_id FROM assessment.results.adoption_section_score ORDER BY run_ts DESC LIMIT 1)
GROUP BY 1

datasets.name: adopt_gaps
queryLines:
SELECT
  section,
  check_id,
  check_name,
  COALESCE(value_display, '') AS measured,
  COALESCE(error, '') AS error
FROM assessment.results.adoption_check_history
WHERE run_id = (SELECT run_id FROM assessment.results.adoption_section_score ORDER BY run_ts DESC LIMIT 1) AND score = 0 AND measurable = TRUE
ORDER BY section, check_id

datasets.name: ds_overall
queryLines:
SELECT
  s.overall_score,
  s.coverage_pct,
  s.confidence,
  s.critical_gaps,
  s.n_measured,
  s.n_not_available,
  s.n_not_applicable,
  s.n_patterns,
  CASE
    WHEN s.overall_score IS NULL THEN 'NOT AVAILABLE'
    WHEN s.overall_score >= 80 THEN 'GOOD'
    WHEN s.overall_score >= 60 THEN 'FAIR'
    ELSE 'POOR'
  END AS conformance_grade,
  r.run_ts,
  r.lookback_days,
  r.registry_version
FROM assessment.results.assessment_score s
JOIN assessment.results.assessment_run r ON r.run_id = s.run_id
WHERE s.run_id = (SELECT run_id FROM assessment.results.assessment_run WHERE status = 'COMPLETE' ORDER BY run_ts DESC LIMIT 1)

datasets.name: ds_category
queryLines:
SELECT
  category,
  ROUND(weighted_score, 1) AS score,
  ROUND(coverage_pct, 1)   AS coverage_pct,
  n_measured,
  n_not_available,
  n_not_applicable,
  n_poor,
  CASE
    WHEN weighted_score IS NULL THEN 'NOT AVAILABLE'
    WHEN weighted_score >= 80 THEN 'GOOD'
    WHEN weighted_score >= 60 THEN 'FAIR'
    ELSE 'POOR'
  END AS implementation
FROM assessment.results.category_score
WHERE run_id = (SELECT run_id FROM assessment.results.assessment_run WHERE status = 'COMPLETE' ORDER BY run_ts DESC LIMIT 1)

datasets.name: ds_checks
queryLines:
SELECT
  category,
  pattern_id,
  title,
  severity,
  grade,
  ROUND(conformance_pct, 1) AS conformance_pct,
  numerator,
  denominator,
  unit,
  finding_count,
  CASE severity WHEN 'CRITICAL' THEN 1 WHEN 'HIGH' THEN 2
                WHEN 'MEDIUM' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END AS severity_rank
FROM assessment.results.v_latest_report
WHERE status = 'MEASURED'
ORDER BY conformance_pct, severity_rank
LIMIT 30

datasets.name: ds_gaps
queryLines:
SELECT
  severity,
  category,
  pattern_id,
  title,
  ROUND(conformance_pct, 1) AS conformance_pct,
  grade,
  floor_pct,
  target_pct,
  CONCAT(CAST(numerator AS STRING), ' / ', CAST(denominator AS STRING), ' ', unit) AS coverage_detail,
  finding_count,
  doc_path
FROM assessment.results.v_latest_report
WHERE status = 'MEASURED' AND grade IN ('POOR', 'FAIR')
ORDER BY
  CASE severity WHEN 'CRITICAL' THEN 1 WHEN 'HIGH' THEN 2
                WHEN 'MEDIUM' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END,
  conformance_pct

datasets.name: ds_findings
queryLines:
SELECT
  f.pattern_id,
  reg.category,
  reg.severity,
  f.object_type,
  f.object_name,
  f.owner,
  f.metric_name,
  f.metric_value,
  -- Relative, so the link works in any workspace. Each object type has
  -- its own console path; anything without one gets NULL and renders as
  -- plain text rather than a link to nowhere.
  CASE
    WHEN f.object_type IN ('TABLE', 'VIEW') AND size(split(f.object_id, '[.]')) = 3
      THEN concat('https://dbc-96494b8f-6b86.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/', replace(f.object_id, '.', '/'), '?o=7474645607548631')
    WHEN f.object_type = 'COLUMN' AND size(split(f.object_id, '[.]')) >= 4
      THEN concat('https://dbc-96494b8f-6b86.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/',
                  array_join(slice(split(f.object_id, '[.]'), 1, 3), '/'), '?o=7474645607548631')
    WHEN f.object_type = 'JOB'        THEN concat('https://dbc-96494b8f-6b86.cloud.databricks.com/jobs/', f.object_id, '?o=7474645607548631')
    WHEN f.object_type = 'JOB_TASK'   THEN concat('https://dbc-96494b8f-6b86.cloud.databricks.com/jobs/', split(f.object_id, ':')[0], '?o=7474645607548631')
    WHEN f.object_type = 'JOB_RUN'    THEN concat('https://dbc-96494b8f-6b86.cloud.databricks.com/jobs/runs/', f.object_id, '?o=7474645607548631')
    WHEN f.object_type = 'EXPERIMENT' THEN concat('https://dbc-96494b8f-6b86.cloud.databricks.com/ml/experiments/', f.object_id, '?o=7474645607548631')
    WHEN f.object_type = 'CLUSTER'    THEN concat('https://dbc-96494b8f-6b86.cloud.databricks.com/compute/clusters/', f.object_id, '?o=7474645607548631')
    WHEN f.object_type = 'PIPELINE'   THEN concat('https://dbc-96494b8f-6b86.cloud.databricks.com/pipelines/', f.object_id, '?o=7474645607548631')
    ELSE NULL
  END AS object_url
FROM assessment.results.check_finding f
JOIN assessment.results.pattern_registry reg
  ON reg.run_id = f.run_id AND reg.pattern_id = f.pattern_id
WHERE f.run_id = (SELECT run_id FROM assessment.results.assessment_run WHERE status = 'COMPLETE' ORDER BY run_ts DESC LIMIT 1)
ORDER BY f.metric_value DESC NULLS LAST

WITH warehouse_snapshot AS ( SELECT warehouse_id, warehouse_name, workspace_id, account_id, change_time, delete_time, CASE WHEN delete_time IS NOT NULL THEN 'Deleted' ELSE 'Active' END AS is_deleted FROM system.compute.warehouses w WHERE -- workspace filter (array_contains(:workspace_id,w.workspace_id) OR array_contains(:workspace_id,'all')) -- warehouse filter AND (array_contains(:warehouse_name, CONCAT(w.warehouse_name, ' (id:', w.warehouse_id, ')')) OR array_contains(:warehouse_name,'all')) QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY workspace_id, warehouse_id ORDER BY change_time DESC) == 1 -- Get more recent snapshot ), root_table AS ( SELECT * FROM assessment.results.dbsql_cost_per_query AS qq WHERE query_attributed_dollars_estimation IS NOT NULL -- workspace filter AND (array_contains(:workspace_id,qq.workspace_id) OR array_contains(:workspace_id,'all')) -- warehouse filter AND (array_contains(:warehouse_id,qq.warehouse_id) OR array_contains(:warehouse_id,'all')) -- time filter (based on query start time) AND query_start_hour BETWEEN CAST(:time_range.min AS TIMESTAMP) AND CAST(:time_range.max AS TIMESTAMP) -- for good pruning -- statement_id filter - optional AND (array_contains(:statement_id,qq.statement_id) OR array_contains(:statement_id,'all')) -- optional statement id filter ), top_n_filter AS ( SELECT IDENTIFIER(CASE WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Executed By' THEN 'executed_by' WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Source Type' THEN 'query_source_type' WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Object Id' THEN 'query_source_id' WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Statement Id' THEN 'statement_id' ELSE 'statement_id' END) AS rank_key, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(query_attributed_dollars_estimation) DESC) AS cost_rank FROM root_table AS qq GROUP BY IDENTIFIER(CASE WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Executed By' THEN 'executed_by' WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Source Type' THEN 'query_source_type' WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Object Id' THEN 'query_source_id' WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Statement Id' THEN 'statement_id' ELSE 'statement_id' END) ), mv_model AS ( SELECT qq.*, CONCAT(w.warehouse_name, ' (id:', w.warehouse_id, ')') AS warehouse_name , w.is_deleted AS is_warehouse_deleted, query_attributed_dollars_estimation * (1 - CAST(:dbsql_discount AS FLOAT)) AS query_attributed_dollars_with_discount, --ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CASE WHEN :ORDER BY QueryAllocationDollars DESC) AS CostRank tn.cost_rank FROM root_table AS qq INNER JOIN warehouse_snapshot w ON qq.workspace_id = w.workspace_id AND qq.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id LEFT JOIN top_n_filter AS tn ON IDENTIFIER(CASE WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Executed By' THEN 'qq.executed_by' WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Source Type' THEN 'qq.query_source_type' WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Object Id' THEN 'qq.query_source_id' WHEN :top_n_dimension = 'Statement Id' THEN 'qq.statement_id' ELSE 'statement_id' END) = tn.rank_key ) SELECT mv.*, CASE WHEN :group_key = 'Warehouse Id' THEN mv.warehouse_id WHEN :group_key = 'Warehouse Name' THEN mv.warehouse_name WHEN :group_key = 'User' THEN mv.executed_by WHEN :group_key = 'Source Type' THEN mv.query_source_type WHEN :group_key = 'Obect Id' THEN mv.query_source_id WHEN :group_key = 'Client' THEN mv.client_application WHEN :group_key = 'Workspace Id' THEN mv.workspace_id END AS group_key, CASE WHEN :date_agg_level = 'HOUR' THEN date_trunc(:date_agg_level, mv.start_time)::timestamp::string ELSE date_trunc(:date_agg_level, mv.start_time)::date::string END AS time_agg_key, -- Data formatting for visuals MAX(query_attributed_dollars_with_discount) OVER() AS fully_loaded_max_usage, MIN(query_attributed_dollars_with_discount) OVER() AS fully_loaded_min_usage, COALESCE(CONCAT( '
', '
', '$', FORMAT_NUMBER(query_attributed_dollars_with_discount, 2), '
' ), '--') AS allocated_dollars_usage_bar_html, -- Data formatting for visuals MAX(query_attributed_dbus_estimation) OVER() AS fully_loaded_max_usage_dbus, MIN(query_attributed_dbus_estimation) OVER() AS fully_loaded_min_usage_dbus, COALESCE(CONCAT( '
', '
', '$', FORMAT_NUMBER(query_attributed_dbus_estimation, 2), '
' ), '--') AS allocated_dbus_usage_bar_html FROM mv_model AS mv WHERE (lower(:top_n)::string = 'all' OR cost_rank <= try_cast(:top_n AS int)) -- There can be ties, so we will also do a limit ORDER BY cost_rank, query_attributed_dollars_with_discount DESC

datasets.name: b6c55fed
datasets.query:
WITH billing AS (
      SELECT workspace_id, usage_metadata.warehouse_id AS warehouse_id
    FROM system.billing.usage u
    WHERE usage_start_time BETWEEN date_trunc('hour', :start_time) AND :end_time
    AND usage_metadata.warehouse_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY 1,2
  )
  -- Get warehouse names (most recent change record) for warehouses with usage in selected period
  SELECT w.workspace_id, w.warehouse_id,   CONCAT(w.warehouse_name, ' (id:', w.warehouse_id, ')') AS warehouse_name
  FROM billing AS b
  JOIN system.compute.warehouses w ON b.workspace_id = w.workspace_id AND w.warehouse_id = b.warehouse_id
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY w.workspace_id, w.warehouse_id ORDER BY w.change_time DESC) == 1

lines:
# Adoption

Which parts of the Databricks platform this workspace actually uses. Each check scores **ACTIVE** (in real use), **MINIMAL** (present, barely used) or **NONE** (no evidence).

This is breadth, not quality. A workspace can use a capability heavily and use it badly — that is a different question, and a different page.

frame.title: Adoption Score
frame.description: Section percentages, weighted by section

frame.title: Adoption Level
frame.description: NOT ADOPTED / EARLY STAGE / PARTIALLY / BROADLY / FULLY LEVERAGED

frame.title: Barely Used
frame.description: Present but minimal

frame.title: Measurable
frame.description: Share of the checklist observable from system tables. The score is computed over these only.

frame.title: Adoption by Section
frame.description: Percentage of available points per platform area, coloured by grade.

frame.title: How Much of the Platform Is Used
frame.description: Every capability checked, by how much it is used. In real use = clear evidence of regular activity. Barely used = switched on but little activity, usually the cheapest gap to close. Not used = no evidence at all.

frame.title: Section Scorecard
frame.description: Weight is each section's share of the overall score.

frame.title: Capabilities Not Used
frame.description: Every capability with no evidence of use — the platform surface being paid for but not exercised. Checks that could not be observed at all are excluded here and from the score; they appear in All Checks as 'not observable'.

frame.title: All Checks
frame.description: Every check, with the value behind each score.

lines:
# Conformance Assessment

**Of the things this workspace does, how well does it do them?**

- **Score** - of the checks we ran, how closely the practice was followed.
- **Coverage** - how many of the checks we could run at all.

**Low coverage is our gap, not the workspace's.** A check with no result is one we could not run - some are not written yet, others need a source the platform does not expose, or judgment a query cannot make. Low coverage means we looked at less, not that the workspace did less.

Practices with nothing to apply to - no clusters to size, no shared data to govern - are left out of both numbers entirely.

frame.title: Conformance Score
frame.description: Severity-weighted % across measured checks

frame.title: Measurement Coverage
frame.description: Severity-weighted % of all checks we could run

frame.title: Critical Gaps
frame.description: CRITICAL-severity checks graded POOR

frame.title: Checks Measured
frame.description: Checks that produced a score

frame.title: Checks Not Available
frame.description: Mostly practices with no check written yet; a few ran and found no data. Coverage page has the split.

frame.title: Implementation by Category
frame.description: Weighted conformance per category, coloured by grade.

frame.title: Measurement Coverage by Category
frame.description: Severity-weighted %. Below 40%, read the score as indicative.

frame.title: Category Scorecard
frame.description: Every category with its grade, score, and how much of it was visible.

lines:
## Findings and Remediation

Checks that produced a measurement, worst first. Grade compares the result against that check's own target and floor.

frame.title: Priority Remediation List
frame.description: Measured checks graded POOR or FAIR, worst severity first. Floor and Target are this check's own thresholds: below Floor is POOR, at or above Target is GOOD. They differ per check, which is why a lower percentage can carry a better grade.

frame.title: 30 Lowest-Scoring Checks
frame.description: Worst first, coloured by grade. Each check has its own floor and target (see the table above), so colour and length do not always agree. Every measured check is in that table; this chart is bounded because a longer one silently drops rows.

frame.title: Evidence
frame.description: The specific objects behind each finding — the remediation worklist. Open goes straight to the table, job or experiment.

frame.title: User
frame.description: User or service principal running the statement

frame.title: Query Source Type
frame.description: Type of Object (i.e dashboard, SQL Query, JOB, notebook)

frame.title: Query Source Id
frame.description: Id of object such as a dashboard, SQL query, job, etc.

columns.title: Query Text
columns.description: Raw text of the statement query that was executed

columns.title: Attributed Usage ($)
columns.description: Allocated dollars for attributed query (this is an estimate based on query work)

columns.title: Warehouse
columns.description: Current name of the warehouse it was run on (warehouse ids are permanent but names are not)

columns.title: Query Duration (s)
columns.description: Runtime of the query in seconds

columns.title: Work Duration (s)
columns.description: Amount of seconds query spent doing work (execution + result fetch)

columns.title: Work Start Time
columns.description: Start time query began doing work (executing) - can be greater than start_time if it waits in the queue

columns.title: Work End Time
columns.description: Time when query finishes work. This can be greater than end_time because it includes time spent returning results.

columns.title: Query Source Type
columns.description: Databricks internal asset source type (i.e. dashboard, notebook, job, etc.)

columns.title: Query Source Id
columns.description: Id of the asset type (i.e. if source type = 'JOB' then this will be the job id that ran the query)

columns.title: Client App
columns.description: External registered client name (like DBSQL Dashboards, Power BI, Fivetran, etc.)

columns.title: Attributed Usage ($) - Discount
columns.description: Estimated query attributed costs with discount param included

columns.title: Attributed Usage ($) - List
columns.description: Estimated query attributed cost at list rate

columns.title: Query Cost Hourly Breakdown
columns.description: If queries span multiple hours, the costs are allocated on an hourly basis, so a total query costs can span multiple hours. This shows what % of the cost is allocated to which hour for that warehouse

# DBSQL Cost Dashboard
-----

### Sections
- **Inputs** - (Mandatory) Choose Start Time and End Time. (Optional) - Can select specific workspaces, warehouses, users, query source types, or object ids (supported for DBX objects). 
  1. If you want to limit the results of the dashboard to top 10 users, you can specify using the "Top N Dimension" and "Top N Number" filters.
  2. Top level counts are shown for reference as you apply different filters. 
- **Charts** - Attributed costs by 1) user 2) source type 3) object ids. If the chart is crowded, click and zoom into the chart, or use the "Top N" filters. Click on a bar to cross-filter across the dashboard (to select multiple filters or options, you will need to back to the inputs at the top) 4) is a time series of attributed usage ($) for the filtered down dataset. Time unit is configurable (daily, weekly, etc). 
  1. Charts can also be downloaded into a CSV file by clicking on the option on the top right corner).
-  **Statement Level Detail** - Attributed usage ($) at the individual SQL run level. 
   1. You can click on the statement id or query source id ("object id") links to manage 
-----
